note: On starting point he is the purest good-to-great prospect in the batch. Eighteen consistent months on a calisthenics programme, pull-ups from near zero to 10-12, 66-68 kg, tracking macros, walking an hour on a treadmill at 5am, and a single residual complaint about abdominal fat. Health is not in crisis and is not being ignored — it is being actively worked — so he passes on severity and passes the deconditioning exclusion by a wide margin. He fails the two commercial criteria. Occupation is simply unknown: the rep established his hours and that he sits all day but never asked what he does, so nothing supports the business-owner-or-physician test. And income fails outright and explicitly — his stated range is $80 to $100 a month against a named competitor, and he closed with 'I don't think I can spend that, that kind of money right now.' This is the sharpest illustration in the batch of the observation already recorded in the ICP file, that 'makes good money' is doing work a payment plan cannot rescue: he wanted it, believed it would work, said it would be a good investment, and was two orders of magnitude away on budget.
